messages:
lin: heads up — after the kernel 6.3.x rollout to a subset of us-west-2 A100 nodes we're seeing p2p disabled on ~30% of the hosts. Affected jobs hit NCCL timeouts and fall back to PCIe which kills throughput.
ajay: which kernel exact? we rolled 6.3.8 to canary yesterday and 6.3.9 to the rest this morning.
maria: saw similar in logs: `dmesg` shows repeated warnings about `BAR1` window size probes failing and `nv_p2p` falling back. sample: `nv_p2p: BAR1 probe returned size 0`
kevin: is this the BAR resizing regression we've seen on Ampere after the new iommu/PCIe patches? might be ACS or ACS override interplay.
lin: exact kernel on failing hosts is 6.3.9-rc2. non-failing ones are still on 6.1.x. drivers still at 525.105.17 for both.
ajay: can we confirm `nvidia-smi topo -m` output? if NVLINK shows missing links that's consistent with P2P disabled.
maria: posted output from a failing node to the thread: ```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
GPU0    GPU1
GPU0    X      PX
GPU1    PX     X
```
(which is wrong for bar1/nvlink expected to be NVLINK or PHB with P2P)
ops: I ran `lspci -vvv` and noticed `PCI bridge: ACS enabled` differences between old and new kernels; some bridges report `ACS: Broken` on new kernels.
kevin: ACS changes would break peer access if the bridge denies upstream direct peer requests. That would force fallback to host-mediated transfers.
ajay: quick ask — can we set `nvidia-igt` tests or a small NCCL ring test on canary set to reproduce and quantify perf regression? I can run a 4xA100 NCCL all-reduce later today.
lin: yes please. also we need telemetry: list of affected instance IDs and whether they're Ampere or A100S. initial sample seems concentrated on older A100-40GB nodes.
maria: put a temporary log grep I used: `dmesg | grep -E \"BAR1|nv_p2p|PCIe\"` — it surfaces the same failures across hosts.
sre-bot: deploy:kernel-6.3.9-rc2 pushed to us-west-2 cluster at 2026-03-17T09:12:34Z — rolling update paused (manual)
ops: tentative mitigations — 1) rollback kernel on subset of hosts to 6.1.x (needs maintenance window) 2) try toggling `pci=nomsi` or kernel cmdline that affects ACS probing 3) update NVIDIA driver to a newer 535 nightly that supposedly has BAR1 probes tolerant code.
kevin: driver upgrade first might be lower blast radius if the driver has a tolerance patch. downside: driver upgrade across fleet also needs node reboot.
lin: cost/throughput impact: fallback to PCIe increases per-job latency by ~3-4x in our perf tests, throughput drops ~60% — means queued jobs extend by hours and we risk hitting committed throughput on Dedicated clusters. Ops, how bad for capacity?
ops: worst-case — if 30% nodes are degraded we need to shift traffic to other regions or burst to cloud reserve; that will increase monthly spend ~18% if sustained. Can try to move low-priority jobs out.
ajay: proposal: (a) run NCCL microbench on 10 canary nodes with 6.3.9+525 to reproduce and gather `nccl-tests` numbers, (b) simultaneously spin up a small pool with upgraded 535 driver on a subset and run same test, (c) if driver fixes it, schedule staged driver rollout with preflight checks.
maria: also add a check to our node-health probe: fail if `nvidia-smi topo -m` doesn't show NVLINK/P2P expected topology, mark node as `no-p2p` to avoid scheduling multi-gpu jobs.
lin: agreed. action items: ajay run nccl-tests on canary today and post results; ops collect list of affected instance IDs + kernel and driver version; kevin research any kernel boot-args that changed ACS behavior between 6.1 and 6.3; maria add health-check PR to mark `no-p2p` nodes.
ops: starting inventory now — will post CSV in the thread.
ajay: kicking off `nccl-tests` now (short runs). will paste numbers when done.
kevin: FYI we should also notify customers on Dedicated that multi-GPU perf may be impacted in us-west-2; low-key heads up via status page with "investigating" until we confirm rollback or driver fix.
lin: good call. I'll draft a brief status blurb after we have initial bench numbers.
maria: PR for health-check ready in my branch, will open PR after I finish test harness.
sre-bot: alert: NCCL_ERROR_TIMEOUT rate increased by 12x in us-west-2 at 09:22 UTC — linked to thread 1902374567
lin: thanks all. we'll reconvene here after ajay's numbers. try to keep any manual rollbacks to a small canary until we have a solid plan. :thumbsup:
